major_concerns: Validator specification undercaptures production safety properties (false sense of safety).
RAG corpus and retrieval tuning may bias results; corpus provenance must be fixed and released.
Synthetic/topology-limited task set may limit external validity across vendors/topologies.
Retry/ rate-limit policy needs strict preregistration to avoid biased reruns.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact deterministic validator (ruleset, Batfish version or equivalent) and share rule corpus prior to runs.
Freeze and publish the RAG corpus, retrieval index, and retrieval method (embedding model, vector store) in preregistration.
Define explicit inclusion/exclusion rules for synthesized topologies and provide seed list for topology generation.
Predefine retry policy for provider/API failures (when a retry is allowed, how outcomes are recorded) and log all retries in execution manifest.

major_concerns: Adversary generator may produce unrealistic/implausible perturbations unless validated against real-world attempts.
Ethical risk: releasing adversary-generation details could enable attack replication—disclosure policy needed.
Deterministic validator may trivially detect many adversarial failures, yielding a null result; that outcome must be reported and interpreted.
Adversary strength calibration and seed control must be rigorous to make comparisons fair.
required_design_repairs: Add an adversary realism validation step (automated heuristics or small expert-reviewed holdout) and preregister its pass/fail criteria.
Include an explicit ethical disclosure/mitigation plan restricting actionable exploit details while preserving reproducibility (e.g., redacted adversary configs with generator code and seeds).
Predefine perturbation-strength metrics and fixed seeds; publish perturbation algorithms and parameters in preregistration.
Clarify whether RAG is enabled/disabled for these runs and freeze retrieval settings.

major_concerns: Simulated automated operator may not reflect human decision-making biases (automation bias, latency).
Provenance scoring heuristics may be experiment-tuned and not generalize; must be fully specified.
Measuring downstream propagation impact requires a clearly articulated simulation model (how flows/impact are computed).
Stripping provenance while keeping 'identical' outputs needs careful artifact management to ensure true pairing.
required_design_repairs: Publish the exact provenance schema and the provenance-confidence scoring algorithm (weights, thresholds) in the preregistration.
Describe and freeze the simulated propagation model used to compute impact metrics (flow definitions, affected resource model).
Define the procedure that produces paired artifacts with/without provenance to guarantee identical textual configs across arms.
Include sensitivity analyses for provenance-threshold choice and preregister the primary threshold(s).

major_concerns: Model confidence proxy (token log-probs or heuristic head) may poorly reflect epistemic uncertainty and vary by provider/model.
Iterative correction may overfit to validator feedback and produce calibration improvements that do not reflect true correctness.
Latency and operational cost of up-to-3 iterations may make improvements impractical even if statistically significant.
Normalization of confidence across runs/providers must be specified to permit fair paired comparisons.
required_design_repairs: Predefine and justify the confidence proxy(s); preregister at least one backup proxy and report both (e.g., token log-prob and calibrated ensemble if available).
Specify normalization procedure for token log-probabilities (per-token normalization, length correction) and freeze it.
Include an analysis plan to detect overfitting-to-validator (e.g., blind out a subset of validator checks for validation of generalization) and preregister it.
Preregister latency budget and assess operational trade-offs; report iteration costs and an acceptability criterion.
